+    def matches(self, values: set[str] | frozenset[str]) -> bool:
+        token = self.peek()

+            and token.value in values

+    def left_chain(self, operand, operators: set[str]) -> Node:

+            self.index += 1
+            node = Binary(operator, node, operand())
+        return node
+
+    def expression(self) -> Node:
+        return self.left_chain(self.and_expression, {"or"})
+
+    def and_expression(self) -> Node:
+        return self.left_chain(self.not_expression, {"and"})
+
+    def not_expression(self) -> Node:

+def _binary(operator: str, left: Value, right: Value) -> Value:
+    if operator in {"==", "!="}:
+        equal = type(left) is type(right) and left == right
+        return equal if operator == "==" else not equal
+    if operator in {"<", "<=", ">", ">="}:
+        if type(left) is not type(right) or type(left) not in {float, str}:
+            raise EvalError(f"{operator} requires two numbers or two strings")
+        if operator == "<":
+            return left < right
+        if operator == "<=":
+            return left <= right
+        if operator == ">":
+            return left > right
+        return left >= right
+    if operator == "+" and type(left) is str and type(right) is str:
+        return left + right
+    a = require_number(left, operator)
+    b = require_number(right, operator)
+    if operator == "+":
+        return a + b
+    if operator == "-":
+        return a - b
+    if operator == "*":
+        return a * b
+    if operator == "/":
+        if b == 0.0:
+            raise EvalError("division by zero")
+        return a / b
+    if operator == "%":
+        if b == 0.0:
+            raise EvalError("modulo by zero")
+        return a % b
+    try:
+        result = a ** b
+    except (OverflowError, ValueError, ZeroDivisionError) as error:
+        raise EvalError(f"invalid exponentiation: {error}") from error
+    if type(result) is not float:
+        raise EvalError("exponentiation result is not a real number")
+    return result
+

+        return node.value

+            raise EvalError(f"undefined variable: {node.name}")
+        value = env[node.name]
+        if type(value) not in {float, str, bool}:
+            raise EvalError(f"unsupported value for {node.name}: {value!r}")
+        return value

+        value = _evaluate(node.operand, env)
+        if node.operator == "not":
+            return not require_boolean(value, "not")

+import re
+import sys
+
+from .builtins import format_value
+from .errors import MiniLangError
+from .evaluator import evaluate
+from .lexer import KEYWORDS
+
+
+ASSIGNMENT = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=(?!=)(.*)$", re.DOTALL)
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    env = {}
+    for line in sys.stdin:
+        command = line.strip()
+        if not command:
+            continue
+        if command == ":quit":
+            return 0
+        if command == ":vars":
+            for name in sorted(env):
+                print(f"{name} = {format_value(env[name])}")
+            continue
+        try:
+            assignment = ASSIGNMENT.match(line)
+            # Reserved keywords are not identifiers, including assignment targets.
+            if assignment is not None and assignment[1] not in KEYWORDS:
+                value = evaluate(assignment[2], env)
+                env[assignment[1]] = value
+            else:
+                print(format_value(evaluate(line, env)))
+        except MiniLangError as error:
+            print(f"error: {error}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+import math

+import minilang

+def run_repl(source):
+    environment = dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1")
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, "-m", "minilang"],
+        input=source,
+        text=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+        env=environment,
+        timeout=10,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0
+    assert result.stderr == ""
+    return result.stdout

+def test_public_api():

+        "MiniLangError", "LexError", "ParseError", "EvalError",

+

+def test_exception_hierarchy_and_plain_messages():

+        error = error_type("plain message", 7)
